transcribed: read from the Cadetprep Excel sheet by extract-cadetprep.ts (sheet row = n); key and solution are the source's, kept as evidence

questions.stem: Two cars are moving towards each other with speeds of \(60 \text{ km/h}\) and \(40 \text{ km/h}\) respectively. What is their relative speed?
questions.keySolution:
When two objects move towards each other, relative speed = Sum of individual speeds
Relative speed = \(60 + 40 = 100 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: A train running at \(54 \text{ km/h}\) overtakes a man walking at \(6 \text{ km/h}\) in the same direction. What is their relative speed?
questions.keySolution:
When objects move in same direction, relative speed = Difference of speeds
Relative speed = \(54 - 6 = 48 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: Two trains each \(150 \text{ m}\) long are moving towards each other at speeds of \(72 \text{ km/h}\) and \(54 \text{ km/h}\). Time taken to cross each other completely is:
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(72 + 54 = 126 \text{ km/h} = 126 \times \frac{5}{18} = 35 \text{ m/s}\)
Total distance = \(150 + 150 = 300 \text{ m}\)
Time = \(\frac{300}{35} = 8.57 \text{ seconds}\)

questions.stem: A boat travels downstream at \(20 \text{ km/h}\) and upstream at \(12 \text{ km/h}\). What is the speed of the stream?
questions.keySolution:
Let boat speed = b, stream speed = s
Downstream: \(b + s = 20\)
Upstream: \(b - s = 12\)
Subtracting: \(2s = 8\), so \(s = 4 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: Two athletes start from opposite ends of a \(400 \text{ m}\) track and run towards each other at speeds of \(8 \text{ m/s}\) and \(12 \text{ m/s}\). When will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(8 + 12 = 20 \text{ m/s}\)
Distance to cover = \(400 \text{ m}\)
Time = \(\frac{400}{20} = 20 \text{ seconds}\)

questions.stem: A faster train takes \(3 \text{ hours}\) to overtake a slower train completely when both are moving in the same direction. If they were moving in opposite directions, they would meet in \(30 \text{ minutes}\). What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.keySolution:
Let speeds be v₁ and v₂ (v₁ > v₂)
Same direction: \((v₁ - v₂) \times 3 = d\)
Opposite direction: \((v₁ + v₂) \times 0.5 = d\)
Solving: \(3(v₁ - v₂) = 0.5(v₁ + v₂)\)
\(6v₁ - 6v₂ = v₁ + v₂\)
\(5v₁ = 7v₂\), so \(v₁:v₂ = 7:5\)

questions.stem: Two cars start from the same point and travel in opposite directions at speeds of \(50 \text{ km/h}\) and \(70 \text{ km/h}\). After how much time will they be \(360 \text{ km}\) apart?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(50 + 70 = 120 \text{ km/h}\)
Distance = \(360 \text{ km}\)
Time = \(\frac{360}{120} = 3 \text{ hours}\)

questions.stem: A train \(200 \text{ m}\) long running at \(60 \text{ km/h}\) overtakes a man running at \(6 \text{ km/h}\) in the same direction. Time taken to pass the man completely:
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(60 - 6 = 54 \text{ km/h} = 54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15 \text{ m/s}\)
Distance = \(200 \text{ m}\) (length of train)
Time = \(\frac{200}{15} = 13.33 \text{ seconds}\)

questions.stem: On a circular track of circumference \(1200 \text{ m}\), two runners start from the same point but in opposite directions at speeds of \(6 \text{ m/s}\) and \(9 \text{ m/s}\). When will they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(6 + 9 = 15 \text{ m/s}\)
Distance = \(1200 \text{ m}\) (circumference)
Time = \(\frac{1200}{15} = 80 \text{ seconds}\)

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths \(100 \text{ m}\) and \(150 \text{ m}\) are running in the same direction at \(45 \text{ km/h}\) and \(36 \text{ km/h}\) respectively. Time for faster train to overtake slower train:
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(45 - 36 = 9 \text{ km/h} = 9 \times \frac{5}{18} = 2.5 \text{ m/s}\)
Total distance = \(100 + 150 = 250 \text{ m}\)
Time = \(\frac{250}{2.5} = 100 \text{ seconds}\)

questions.stem: A thief steals a car and drives at \(80 \text{ km/h}\). A policeman starts chasing \(2 \text{ hours}\) later at \(100 \text{ km/h}\). When will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.keySolution:
Thief's head start = \(80 \times 2 = 160 \text{ km}\)
Relative speed = \(100 - 80 = 20 \text{ km/h}\)
Time to catch = \(\frac{160}{20} = 8 \text{ hours}\)

questions.stem: Two persons A and B start walking towards each other from points \(20 \text{ km}\) apart. A walks at \(4 \text{ km/h}\) and B at \(6 \text{ km/h}\). After how long will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(4 + 6 = 10 \text{ km/h}\)
Distance = \(20 \text{ km}\)
Time = \(\frac{20}{10} = 2 \text{ hours}\)

questions.stem: A train crosses a platform \(300 \text{ m}\) long in \(39 \text{ seconds}\) and crosses a signal pole in \(18 \text{ seconds}\). Find the speed of the train.
questions.keySolution:
Let train length = L
From pole crossing: \(L = 18 \times v\)
From platform crossing: \(L + 300 = 39 \times v\)
Subtracting: \(300 = 21v\), so \(v = \frac{300}{21} = 14.29 \text{ m/s} = 51.43 \text{ km/h} \approx 60 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: Two cyclists start from the same point and ride in the same direction. The first rides at \(12 \text{ km/h}\) and the second at \(8 \text{ km/h}\). How far apart will they be after \(3 \text{ hours}\)?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(12 - 8 = 4 \text{ km/h}\)
Time = \(3 \text{ hours}\)
Distance apart = \(4 \times 3 = 12 \text{ km}\)

questions.stem: A boat's speed in still water is \(15 \text{ km/h}\). If the boat takes the same time to travel \(20 \text{ km}\) downstream and \(10 \text{ km}\) upstream, find the stream speed.
questions.keySolution:
Let stream speed = s
Time downstream = \(\frac{20}{15+s}\)
Time upstream = \(\frac{10}{15-s}\)
Equating: \(\frac{20}{15+s} = \frac{10}{15-s}\)
Solving: \(20(15-s) = 10(15+s)\)
\(300-20s = 150+10s\)
\(150 = 30s\), so \(s = 5 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: Two trains start simultaneously from stations A and B towards each other. Train from A runs at \(80 \text{ km/h}\) and from B at \(60 \text{ km/h}\). If distance between A and B is \(280 \text{ km}\), when will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(80 + 60 = 140 \text{ km/h}\)
Distance = \(280 \text{ km}\)
Time = \(\frac{280}{140} = 2 \text{ hours}\)

questions.stem: A man walks at \(5 \text{ km/h}\). A train \(110 \text{ m}\) long overtakes him in \(10 \text{ seconds}\). Find the speed of the train.
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(\frac{110}{10} = 11 \text{ m/s} = 11 \times \frac{18}{5} = 39.6 \text{ km/h}\)
Train speed = \(39.6 + 5 = 44.6 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: Two cars leave from the same point in opposite directions at \(9 \text{ AM}\). Car A travels at \(60 \text{ km/h}\) and Car B at \(80 \text{ km/h}\). At what time will they be \(350 \text{ km}\) apart?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(60 + 80 = 140 \text{ km/h}\)
Time = \(\frac{350}{140} = 2.5 \text{ hours}\)
They will be 350 km apart at \(9:00 + 2:30 = 11:30 \text{ AM}\)

questions.stem: On a circular track, two runners start from diametrically opposite points and run in the same direction. If the track circumference is \(400 \text{ m}\) and their speeds are \(8 \text{ m/s}\) and \(6 \text{ m/s}\), when will the faster runner lap the slower one?
questions.keySolution:
Initial gap = \(\frac{400}{2} = 200 \text{ m}\)
Relative speed = \(8 - 6 = 2 \text{ m/s}\)
Time to make up initial gap = \(\frac{200}{2} = 100 \text{ seconds}\)
Time for complete lap = \(\frac{400}{2} = 200 \text{ seconds}\)
Total time = \(100 + 100 = 200 \text{ seconds}\)

questions.stem: A train \(240 \text{ m}\) long crosses a bridge \(360 \text{ m}\) long in \(40 \text{ seconds}\). What is the speed of the train?
questions.keySolution:
Total distance = \(240 + 360 = 600 \text{ m}\)
Time = \(40 \text{ seconds}\)
Speed = \(\frac{600}{40} = 15 \text{ m/s} = 15 \times \frac{18}{5} = 54 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: Two motorcyclists start from the same point and travel in the same direction at \(40 \text{ km/h}\) and \(60 \text{ km/h}\). After \(2 \text{ hours}\), how far apart are they?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(60 - 40 = 20 \text{ km/h}\)
Time = \(2 \text{ hours}\)
Distance apart = \(20 \times 2 = 40 \text{ km}\)

questions.stem: A river flows at \(2 \text{ km/h}\). A boat travels \(10 \text{ km}\) upstream and returns downstream. If the total journey time is \(4.2 \text{ hours}\) and boat speed in still water is constant, find boat speed.
questions.keySolution:
Let boat speed = b
Time upstream = \(\frac{10}{b-2}\)
Time downstream = \(\frac{10}{b+2}\)
Total time: \(\frac{10}{b-2} + \frac{10}{b+2} = 4.2\)
Solving: \(\frac{10(b+2) + 10(b-2)}{(b-2)(b+2)} = 4.2\)
\(\frac{20b}{b^2-4} = 4.2\)
\(20b = 4.2(b^2-4)\)
Solving gives b = 5 km/h

questions.stem: Two trains of equal length take \(10 \text{ seconds}\) to cross each other when running in opposite directions and \(50 \text{ seconds}\) when running in the same direction. Find the ratio of their speeds.
questions.keySolution:
Let speeds be v₁ and v₂, train length = L
Opposite: \(\frac{2L}{v_1+v_2} = 10\), so \(v_1+v_2 = \frac{L}{5}\)
Same direction: \(\frac{2L}{v_1-v_2} = 50\), so \(v_1-v_2 = \frac{L}{25}\)
Solving: \(v_1 = \frac{3L}{50}\), \(v_2 = \frac{L}{50}\)
Ratio \(v_1:v_2 = 3:2\)

questions.stem: A person walks from A to B at \(4 \text{ km/h}\) and returns from B to A at \(6 \text{ km/h}\). If the total time for round trip is \(5 \text{ hours}\), find distance AB.
questions.keySolution:
Let distance AB = d
Time A to B = \(\frac{d}{4}\)
Time B to A = \(\frac{d}{6}\)
Total time: \(\frac{d}{4} + \frac{d}{6} = 5\)
\(\frac{3d+2d}{12} = 5\)
\(\frac{5d}{12} = 5\)
\(d = 12 \text{ km}\)

questions.stem: On a \(200 \text{ m}\) circular track, two athletes start simultaneously from the same point in opposite directions at \(5 \text{ m/s}\) and \(3 \text{ m/s}\). How many times do they cross each other in \(2 \text{ minutes}\)?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(5 + 3 = 8 \text{ m/s}\)
Time for one crossing = \(\frac{200}{8} = 25 \text{ seconds}\)
Total time = \(2 \text{ minutes} = 120 \text{ seconds}\)
Number of crossings = \(\frac{120}{25} = 4.8 \approx 5\)
Including start meeting, total meetings = 6

questions.stem: A train running at \(72 \text{ km/h}\) crosses a man walking at \(8 \text{ km/h}\) in opposite direction in \(6 \text{ seconds}\). Length of the train is:
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(72 + 8 = 80 \text{ km/h} = 80 \times \frac{5}{18} = 22.22 \text{ m/s}\)
Length of train = \(22.22 \times 6 = 133.33 \text{ m}\)

questions.stem: Two cars start from points A and B simultaneously towards each other. They meet after \(4 \text{ hours}\). If car from A had started \(1 \text{ hour}\) earlier, they would have met after \(3 \text{ hours}\) 36 minutes from the start of car B. Find speed ratio of cars.
questions.keySolution:
Let speeds be v_A and v_B, distance = d
Case 1: \(4(v_A + v_B) = d\)
Case 2: \(5v_A + 3.6v_B = d\)
From equations: \(4v_A + 4v_B = 5v_A + 3.6v_B\)
\(0.4v_B = v_A\)
Therefore, \(v_A:v_B = 5:4\)

questions.stem: A boat goes \(24 \text{ km}\) upstream and \(28 \text{ km}\) downstream in \(6 \text{ hours}\). It goes \(30 \text{ km}\) upstream and \(21 \text{ km}\) downstream in \(6.5 \text{ hours}\). Find boat speed in still water.

Two trains start from stations \(200 \text{ km}\) apart at the same time towards each other. One travels at \(60 \text{ km/h}\), the other at \(40 \text{ km/h}\). A bird starts from the faster train and flies back and forth between the trains until they meet. If bird flies at \(80 \text{ km/h}\), what distance does it cover?
questions.keySolution:
Time for trains to meet = \(\frac{200}{60+40} = 2 \text{ hours}\)
Bird flies continuously for 2 hours at 80 km/h
Distance covered by bird = \(80 \times 2 = 160 \text{ km}\)

questions.stem: A cyclist covers a certain distance at \(12 \text{ km/h}\) and returns at \(8 \text{ km/h}\). If total time is \(5 \text{ hours}\), find the distance of one way.
questions.keySolution:
Let distance = d
Time = \(\frac{d}{12} + \frac{d}{8} = 5\)
\(\frac{2d + 3d}{24} = 5\)
\(\frac{5d}{24} = 5\)
\(d = 24 \text{ km}\) for round trip
One way = \(\frac{24}{2} = 12 \text{ km}\)

questions.stem: A train \(180 \text{ m}\) long crosses another train \(120 \text{ m}\) long coming from opposite direction in \(6 \text{ seconds}\). If speed of first train is \(60 \text{ km/h}\), find speed of second train.
questions.keySolution:
Total distance = \(180 + 120 = 300 \text{ m}\)
Relative speed = \(\frac{300}{6} = 50 \text{ m/s} = 180 \text{ km/h}\)
Speed of first train = 60 km/h
Speed of second train = \(180 - 60 = 120 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: Two friends start walking towards each other from two places \(15 \text{ km}\) apart. They meet after \(1.5 \text{ hours}\). If one walks \(1 \text{ km/h}\) faster than the other, find their speeds.
questions.keySolution:
Let speeds be v and (v+1)
Relative speed = v + (v+1) = 2v + 1
Distance = 15 km, Time = 1.5 hours
\(2v + 1 = \frac{15}{1.5} = 10\)
\(2v = 9\), so \(v = 4.5 \text{ km/h}\)
Speeds are 4.5 km/h and 5.5 km/h

questions.stem: A man rows \(16 \text{ km}\) downstream in \(2 \text{ hours}\) and \(12 \text{ km}\) upstream in \(3 \text{ hours}\). Find his rowing speed in still water.
questions.keySolution:
Downstream speed = \(\frac{16}{2} = 8 \text{ km/h}\)
Upstream speed = \(\frac{12}{3} = 4 \text{ km/h}\)
Rowing speed = \(\frac{8+4}{2} = 6 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: Two buses leave a station at the same time in opposite directions. After \(3 \text{ hours}\), they are \(420 \text{ km}\) apart. If one bus travels \(10 \text{ km/h}\) faster than the other, find their speeds.
questions.keySolution:
Let speeds be v and (v+10)
Relative speed = v + (v+10) = 2v + 10
Distance = 420 km, Time = 3 hours
\(2v + 10 = \frac{420}{3} = 140\)
\(2v = 130\), so \(v = 65 \text{ km/h}\)
Speeds are 65 km/h and 75 km/h

questions.stem: A train crosses a \(150 \text{ m}\) long platform in \(15 \text{ seconds}\) and a \(250 \text{ m}\) long platform in \(20 \text{ seconds}\). Find the length and speed of the train.
questions.keySolution:
Let train length = L, speed = v
\(L + 150 = 15v\) ... (1)
\(L + 250 = 20v\) ... (2)
Subtracting: \(100 = 5v\), so \(v = 20 \text{ m/s} = 72 \text{ km/h}\)
From (1): \(L = 15 \times 20 - 150 = 150 \text{ m}\)

questions.stem: In a \(100 \text{ m}\) race, A beats B by \(10 \text{ m}\) and B beats C by \(5 \text{ m}\). By how much does A beat C in the same race?
questions.keySolution:
When A completes 100m, B covers 90m
When B completes 100m, C covers 95m
When A completes 100m:
B covers 90m
C covers \(\frac{95}{100} \times 90 = 85.5 \text{ m}\)
A beats C by \(100 - 85.5 = 14.5 \text{ m}\)

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths \(120 \text{ m}\) and \(80 \text{ m}\) approach each other on parallel tracks at speeds of \(54 \text{ km/h}\) and \(36 \text{ km/h}\). How long do they take to completely cross each other?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(54 + 36 = 90 \text{ km/h} = 25 \text{ m/s}\)
Total length = \(120 + 80 = 200 \text{ m}\)
Time = \(\frac{200}{25} = 8 \text{ seconds}\)

questions.stem: A person travels equal distances at speeds of \(3 \text{ km/h}\), \(4 \text{ km/h}\) and \(6 \text{ km/h}\). Find his average speed for the entire journey.
questions.keySolution:
Let each distance = d
Time₁ = \(\frac{d}{3}\), Time₂ = \(\frac{d}{4}\), Time₃ = \(\frac{d}{6}\)
Total time = \(d(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6}) = d \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{3d}{4}\)
Total distance = 3d
Average speed = \(\frac{3d}{\frac{3d}{4}} = 4 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: A man can row at \(8 \text{ km/h}\) in still water. The river current is \(2 \text{ km/h}\). How much time will he take to go \(15 \text{ km}\) downstream and return?
questions.keySolution:
Downstream speed = \(8 + 2 = 10 \text{ km/h}\)
Upstream speed = \(8 - 2 = 6 \text{ km/h}\)
Time downstream = \(\frac{15}{10} = 1.5 \text{ hours}\)
Time upstream = \(\frac{15}{6} = 2.5 \text{ hours}\)
Total time = \(1.5 + 2.5 = 4 \text{ hours}\)

questions.stem: Two cars start from the same point at the same time and travel in the same direction at \(50 \text{ km/h}\) and \(60 \text{ km/h}\). When will they be \(30 \text{ km}\) apart?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(60 - 50 = 10 \text{ km/h}\)
Distance = \(30 \text{ km}\)
Time = \(\frac{30}{10} = 3 \text{ hours}\)

questions.stem: A train running at \(45 \text{ km/h}\) crosses a bridge in \(30 \text{ seconds}\). The same train crosses a signal post in \(18 \text{ seconds}\). What is the length of the bridge?
questions.keySolution:
Speed = \(45 \text{ km/h} = 45 \times \frac{5}{18} = 12.5 \text{ m/s}\)
Length of train = \(12.5 \times 18 = 225 \text{ m}\)
Train + Bridge = \(12.5 \times 30 = 375 \text{ m}\)
Bridge length = \(375 - 225 = 150 \text{ m}\)

questions.stem: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of \(100 \text{ m}\). When the policeman starts chasing, both run at \(10 \text{ km/h}\) and \(8 \text{ km/h}\) respectively. How far will the thief run before being caught?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(10 - 8 = 2 \text{ km/h} = \frac{5}{9} \text{ m/s}\)
Time to catch = \(\frac{100}{\frac{5}{9}} = 180 \text{ seconds}\)
Thief's speed = \(8 \text{ km/h} = \frac{20}{9} \text{ m/s}\)
Distance run by thief = \(\frac{20}{9} \times 180 = 400 \text{ m}\)

questions.stem: Two cyclists start from opposite ends of a \(60 \text{ km}\) road and cycle towards each other at \(15 \text{ km/h}\) and \(20 \text{ km/h}\). A fly starts from the faster cyclist and flies back and forth at \(25 \text{ km/h}\) until the cyclists meet. What distance does the fly cover?
questions.keySolution:
Time for cyclists to meet = \(\frac{60}{15+20} = \frac{60}{35} = \frac{12}{7} \text{ hours}\)
Fly travels continuously at 25 km/h for this time
Distance covered by fly = \(25 \times \frac{12}{7} = \frac{300}{7} = 42.86 \text{ km}\)

questions.stem: A boat takes \(3 \text{ hours}\) to travel \(30 \text{ km}\) downstream and \(5 \text{ hours}\) to travel \(25 \text{ km}\) upstream. Find the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the current.
questions.keySolution:
Downstream speed = \(\frac{30}{3} = 10 \text{ km/h}\)
Upstream speed = \(\frac{25}{5} = 5 \text{ km/h}\)
Boat speed = \(\frac{10+5}{2} = 7.5 \text{ km/h}\)
Current speed = \(\frac{10-5}{2} = 2.5 \text{ km/h}\)

questions.stem: On a circular track of \(400 \text{ m}\), two runners start at the same time from the same point in the same direction at \(4 \text{ m/s}\) and \(6 \text{ m/s}\). When will the faster runner lap the slower runner for the second time?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(6 - 4 = 2 \text{ m/s}\)
Time for one lap = \(\frac{400}{2} = 200 \text{ seconds}\)
For second time lapping = \(2 \times 200 = 400 \text{ seconds}\)
